title: What If the Mediterranean Sea Dried Up?

scenes.text: What if the Mediterranean dried up? Earth already ran that experiment.
About six million years ago, cut off from the Atlantic, it shrank until its floor lay three to five kilometers below sea level.
Rivers cut to match. Beneath the Nile, north of Cairo, a canyon plunged about two and a half kilometers.
The drying took roughly a thousand years and left a thick layer of salt across the whole basin.
Then the Atlantic broke through at Gibraltar, pouring in around a hundred million cubic meters of water every second.
At its peak the sea may have risen ten meters a day. Most of the basin refilled in two years or less.

description:
What if the Mediterranean Sea dried up?
It did, about six million years ago, then refilled in one of the biggest floods Earth has seen.
